text: Fibonacci is the sequence where every number is the sum of the two before it, and we'll build it in eight lines.
The signature says it all — take an integer n, hand back a list of integers.
A docstring on line two documents what the function does for whoever reads it next.
We seed the list with zero and one, because the sequence needs two numbers before it can grow.
Then we loop while the list is still shorter than n — that's our stopping condition.
Each pass appends the sum of the last two entries. Minus one is the final item, minus two the one before it.
Negative indexing reads from the end backwards, so this stays readable however long the list gets.
The final slice quietly handles the edge case where n is smaller than two.
And printing the first ten shows that classic curve — small, then suddenly not.
